title: A module that is the directed union of flat modules over directed subrings is flat
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $(R_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ a family of subrings of $R$ indexed by a nonempty set $\Lambda$ with a partial order such that $R_\lambda\subseteq R_\mu$ for $\lambda\le\mu$, any two elements of $\Lambda$ have an upper bound, and $R= igcup_\lambda R_\lambda$. Let $M$ be an $R$-module (an $R_\lambda$-module by restriction of scalars for every $\lambda$). For every $\lambda$ let $M_\lambda$ be an $R_\lambda$-module and $\iota_\lambda:M_\lambda	o M$ an $R_\lambda$-linear map, and for $\lambda\le\mu$ let $t_{\lambda\mu}:M_\lambda	o M_\mu$ be an $R_\lambda$-linear map, such that $t_{\lambda\lambda}=\mathrm{id}$, $t_{\mu
u}\circ t_{\lambda\mu}=t_{\lambda
u}$ for $\lambda\le\mu\le
u$, and $\iota_\mu\circ t_{\lambda\mu}=\iota_\lambda$ for $\lambda\le\mu$. Assume (i) every element of $M$ is $\iota_\lambda(m)$ for some $\lambda$ and some $m\in M_\lambda$, and (ii) if $m\in M_\lambda$ and $\iota_\lambda(m)=0$, then $t_{\lambda\mu}(m)=0$ for some $\mu\ge\lambda$. If $M_\lambda$ is a flat $R_\lambda$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] for every $\lambda$, then $M$ is a flat $R$-module.

proof.text: Apply the backward equational criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-equational-criterion]. Given a finite relation ∑ₖ rₖ mₖ = 0 in M, use the union hypothesis to choose stages for the coefficients and h_repr to choose stage representatives for the elements. The finite union of these sets of indices has an upper bound i by directedness and nonemptiness, including when the relation is empty. Move coefficients and representatives to stage i. Naturality gives ιᵢ(yₖ) = mₖ.

The stage-i relation s = ∑ₖ aₖ yₖ has ιᵢ(s) = 0 by linearity and the original relation. Apply h_zero to s: there are j ≥ i and tᵢⱼ(s) = 0. Linearity of tᵢⱼ for the restricted scalar action gives ∑ₖ bₖ zₖ = 0 in Mⱼ, where bₖ is the inclusion of aₖ into Rⱼ and zₖ = tᵢⱼ(yₖ). Naturality still gives ιⱼ(zₖ) = mₖ.

By hflat j and the forward equational criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-equational-criterion], choose a finite matrix cₖₛ over Rⱼ and elements qₛ of Mⱼ with zₖ = ∑ₛ cₖₛ qₛ and ∑ₖ bₖ cₖₛ = 0. Applying ιⱼ to the first equations gives mₖ = ∑ₛ cₖₛ ιⱼ(qₛ), with coefficients now in R. Applying the subring inclusion Rⱼ → R to the second equations gives ∑ₖ rₖ cₖₛ = 0. This trivializes the original relation and closes the backward criterion.

lean.statement: theorem directedUnionSubrings_flat_module {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {Λ : Type v} [PartialOrder Λ] [Nonempty Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)] (Rsub : Λ → Subring R) (hR : ∀ {i j : Λ}, i ≤ j → Rsub i ≤ Rsub j) (hUnion : (Set.univ : Set R) = ⋃ i, (Rsub i : Set R)) {M : Type w} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] (Mstage : ∀ i : Λ, Type x) (instAdd : ∀ i : Λ, AddCommMonoid (Mstage i)) (instMod : ∀ i : Λ, Module (Rsub i) (Mstage i)) (ι : ∀ i : Λ, letI : Module (Rsub i) M := Module.compHom M (Rsub i).subtype Mstage i →ₗ[Rsub i] M) (t : ∀ {i j : Λ} (h : i ≤ j), letI : Module (Rsub i) (Mstage j) := Module.compHom (Mstage j) (Subring.inclusion (hR h)) Mstage i →ₗ[Rsub i] Mstage j) (t_id : ∀ (i : Λ) (x : Mstage i), t (le_refl i) x = x) (t_comp : ∀ {i j k : Λ} (h₁ : i ≤ j) (h₂ : j ≤ k) (x : Mstage i), t h₂ (t h₁ x) = t (h₁.trans h₂) x) (ι_naturality : ∀ {i j : Λ} (h : i ≤ j) (x : Mstage i), ι j (t h x) = ι i x) (h_repr : ∀ m : M, ∃ (i : Λ) (x : Mstage i), ι i x = m) (h_zero : ∀ {i : Λ} (x : Mstage i), ι i x = 0 → ∃ j : Λ, ∃ h : i ≤ j, t h x = 0) (hflat : ∀ i : Λ, Module.Flat (Rsub i) (Mstage i)) : Module.Flat R M
